column3: The initial Hebrew verb is feminine singular, with Miriam named before Aaron.
The Hebrew asks whether the LORD has spoken through them, rather than using present-tense “Does He speak.”
The Hebrew says both came out, rather than stepped forward.
The Hebrew says “mouth to mouth,” rather than “face to face.” It repeats “against” before Moses’ name.
The Hebrew repeats Miriam’s name when Aaron turns toward her and says “behold” twice; it does not separately add “white.”
The Hebrew separately states that they acted foolishly and that they sinned.
The Hebrew says “like one dead,” without separately naming a stillborn infant.
